overview: The chat message packet carries every chat line and command the player types, which makes it the input surface for chat spam, captcha systems and text-based exploit attempts. Server-side anticheats split into two families: event-based chat systems that hook the Bukkit chat pipeline, and raw packet checks that validate the message bytes before the server processes them. The packet also carries the commands that log4j and similar exploits are delivered through, so payload scanning of chat is a standard mitigation.

checks.name: ChatB (Grim)
checks.purpose: Rejects chat messages and commands that the vanilla server would never accept, closing the spigot antispam bypass.
checks.how_it_works: PreViaPacketReceiveListener that decodes CHAT_MESSAGE, CHAT_COMMAND and CHAT_COMMAND_UNSIGNED. A chat message is invalid if it is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or starts with / on 1.19+ where commands have their own packet. Commands are invalid if they carry trailing or surrounding whitespace. On flag it cancels the packet and calls onPacketCancel so downstream state stays consistent. The comment notes click-event edge cases can false flag on badly configured servers.
checks.detects: Empty or whitespace-padded chat messages, spigot antispam bypasses that smuggle text via formatting, and malformed command packets.
checks.variations: BetterAnticheat ImpossibleMessageCheck flags empty and space-prefixed messages, Photon ImpossibleChat flags chat while sprinting or in an inventory, and Kauri Log4J scans the message for JNDI syntax.

checks.name: ChatListener (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: The classic chat pipeline: captcha, text spam, command spam, relog and login-rate checks dispatched from the Bukkit chat events.
checks.how_it_works: CheckListener that wires the Captcha, Commands, Logins, Text and Relog checks and registers ChatConfig and ChatData. AsyncPlayerChatEvent at LOWEST priority runs the Text check and cancels spam; PlayerCommandPreprocessEvent at LOWEST runs the command checks with left-trimmed messages and command alias resolution; PlayerLoginEvent runs captcha reset, fast relog and login-rate checks. It also records teleport-like commands for the net checks and maintains prefix trees for ignored and chat-handled commands.
checks.detects: Chat spam, command spam, captcha evasion, fast re-logging and login flooding.
checks.variations: Photon ImpossibleChat runs on AsyncPlayerChatEvent too, Grim and BetterAnticheat validate the raw packet instead, and Kauri filters JNDI patterns from the chat stream.

checks.name: ImpossibleMessageCheck (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Flags chat messages that cannot exist: fully empty or space-only strings and messages starting with a space.
checks.how_it_works: handleReceivePlayPacket reads WrapperPlayClientChatMessage and checks the raw string: a trim that is empty fails with the code emp, a leading space fails with the code spc. Failures are recorded through the check base with the short codes as data.
checks.detects: Empty chat packets and space-prefixed messages used to bypass spam filters.
checks.variations: Grim ChatB also requires the message to be trim-equal and rejects / prefixes on modern versions; Photon ImpossibleChat covers the behavioral side instead.

checks.name: Log4J (Kauri)
checks.purpose: Scans chat messages for the JNDI lookup syntax used by the log4j exploit and cancels the packet.
checks.how_it_works: WCancellable bound to WrapperPlayClientChatMessage. It compiles the pattern \$\{.*} and, if the whole message matches, flags 'Tried to use JNDI exploit' and returns true to cancel; otherwise it debug-logs the message and lets it through.
checks.variations: Intave filters the same syntax in its CommandFilter and Log4JExploitFilter modules; Grim and BetterAnticheat validate chat shape rather than content.

checks.name: ImpossibleChat (Photon)
checks.purpose: Flags chat sent while the player is in a state where the client physically cannot be chatting: sprinting, sneaking, blocking, dead, or inside a long-open inventory.
checks.how_it_works: EventListener on AsyncPlayerChatEvent. If the user is sprinting, sneaking, blocking, dead, or has had an inventory open for over a second, it flags with +25 VL and cancels the event at the configured cancel VL (default 75). Violation management decays 25 VL every 600 ms.
checks.detects: Chat modules that send messages while the client is in an impossible state, and inventory-based chat bypasses.
checks.variations: Grim ChatC flags moving while chatting from the raw packet stream; NoCheatPlus runs its Text and Captcha checks on the same event.
